COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
SPA/156/2022
Randhir Singh Panwar
--Petitioner
 Versus
Contentment Board Dehradun
--Respondent
Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Gupta, C. J.
Hon’ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
1. Mr. U.K.Uniyal, learned Senior Counsel 
assisted by Mr. Sandeep Kothari, learned 
counsel for the appellant. 
2. Mr. Bhagwat Mehra, learned counsel for 
the respondents no. 1 to 3. 
3. Mr. Krishna Mohan Joshi, learned 
counsel, holding brief of Mr. V.K.Kaparwan, 
learned counsel for the respondent no. 
4/Union of India.
4. Mr. U. K. Uniyal, learned senior counsel 
appearing for the appellant contends that the 
original testimonials were submitted by the 
appellant before the Cantonment Board along 
with letter dated 23.04.2001 (at page 179 of 
the paper book). In support of the said plea, 
he has placed reliance on paragraphs 4, 5 & 6 
of the affidavit along with which the said 
covering letter was filed. In reply to the 
affidavit, the Cantonment Board in para 9 has 
stated that annexure-2, the covering letter  appears to be a manipulated and procured 
document. 
5. We observe that the covering letter 
dated 23.04.2001 bears a stamp of receipt of 
said letter by the Cantonment Board. It also 
bears Dispatch No. 290, dated 23.04.2001. 
6. The appellant has been dismissed from 
service primarily on the ground that 
testimonials on basis of which he procured the 
appointment appears to be fake documents as 
the original certificates have not been 
produced. Therefore, we direct the 
Cantonment Board to place before us the 
relevant Dispatch register so that it could be 
ascertained whether the original testimonials 
were submitted by the appellant before the 
Cantonment Board.
7. List on 12.05.2026. 
8. Learned counsel for the Cantonment 
Board undertakes to produce the relevant 
Dispatch and Receipt registers on the next 
date. 
(Subhash Upadhyay, J.)(Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.) 
 15.04.2026 15.04.2026

11.08.2026 UKHC010086342022
SPA/156/2022
Randhir Singh Panwar
--Appellant
 Versus
Contentment Board Dehradun & Ors.
--Respondents
Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Gupta, C. J.
Hon’ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
1. Mr. U.K. Uniyal, learned Senior Counsel (through V.C.) 
assisted by Mr. Sandeep Kothari, learned counsel for the 
appellant.
2. Mr. Bhagwat Mehra, learned counsel for respondent 
no.1, 2 and 3/Cantonment Board.
3. Mr. V.K. Kaparuwan, learned Standing Counsel for 
respondent no.4 through V.C.
4. In compliance of our previous order, the original 
receipt register of Cantonment Board has been placed before 
us and from perusal whereof it transpires that the letter 
dated 23.04.2001 (at page no.179 of the writ petition) was 
duly received in the Cantonment Office on the same date. 
However, Shri Bhagwat Mehra, learned counsel appearing for 
the Cantonment Board submits that the endorsement made 
on the said register to the effect: (Degree M.A. No.-
1300021) had been made subsequently. He submits that 
the clerk who had put his signatures acknowledging receipt 
of the said letter though retired is still alive and he is ready 
to testify that the endorsement made within brackets was 
added subsequently. 
5. We find that during course of disciplinary proceedings, 
the Board got the testimonials of the petitioner verified from 
Hemvati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University. The 
University, by a communication dated 04.03.2015, informed 
the Chief Executive Officer, Cantonment Board, Dehradun 
that there is no mention of award of any such degree of M.A. 
or B.Ed. to the petitioner in the records of the University. On 
account of the said reason, the University informed the  Cantonment Board that it is not possible for it to verify the 
correctness of the testimonials. 
6. We observe that the University, while informing the 
Cantonment Board that there is no mention of the 
testimonials in its record, has not disclosed the records 
which were looked into. 
7. According to learned counsel appearing for the 
Cantonment Board, the marks obtained by every candidate 
appearing in any examination of the University are recorded 
in a cross register/dummy list. Dr. Kartikey Hari Gupta, 
learned counsel for the University, on request of the Court, is 
present. He states that he will get all necessary registers and 
records pertaining to the examinations in question, details of 
which are as follows:-
1. Mark sheet of M.A. Previous 
Examination (Sociology) 1993
Roll No.M-3924681
Enrollment No. G9240113
2. Mark sheet of M.A. Final 
Examination (Sociology) 1994
Roll No.607315
Enrolment No.G 9240113
3. Master Degree in the 
Examination of 1994 in Sociology 
dated 11.04.2001
Roll No.607315
4. Degree of Bachelor of Education 
in the Examination of 1996 dated 
19.3.1998
Roll No.E 4441566
8. As the entire controversy hinges on the sole issue as 
to whether the petitioner had the requisite qualification at 
the time he was appointed on the post of Junior Lecturer (re￾designated as Lecturer) or he procured appointment on basis 
of fake testimonials, which are now alleged to have been 
lost, we request learned counsel for the University to 
produce the relevant registers/documents in respect of the 
said examinations on the next date. 
9. The original register has been returned to learned 
counsel for the Cantonment Board. 
10. List on 31.08.2026.
(Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.) 
 11.08.2026 11.08.2026
Rajni

31.08.2026 UKHC010086342022
SPA/156/2022
Randhir Singh Panwar --Appellant
 Versus
Contentment Board Dehradun and Others
--Respondents
Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Gupta, C. J.
Hon’ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
1. Mr. U.K. Uniyal, learned Senior Counsel (through 
V.C.) assisted by Mr. Sandeep Kothari, learned counsel 
for the appellant.
2. Mr. Bhagwat Mehra, learned counsel for respondent 
nos.1, 2 and 3/ Cantonment Board.
3. Mr. Rajesh Sharma, learned Standing Counsel for 
the Union of India/ respondent no.4.
4. Dr. K.H. Gupta, learned counsel appearing for the 
Hemvati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University.
5. Pursuant to our previous order dated 11.08.2026,
Dr. K.H. Gupta, learned counsel for the university 
(Hemvati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University) has 
produced before us the original enrolment register of the 
year 1993, the year in which the appellant had allegedly 
taken admission in M.A. (Sociology). The register does 
not contain any application by the appellant for his 
enrollment in the said course nor his enrollment 
certificate.
6. As far as the register wherein the degree issued to 
the students is recorded, the same has not been 
produced before us. Dr. K.H. Gupta, learned counsel for 
the university states that the said register is not 
traceable.
7. Photocopy of marks tabulation register of M.A. Part￾I (Sociology) and M.A. Part-II (Sociology) of the relevant  years have also been produced before us.
8. Dr. K.H. Gupta states that the original is in custody 
of C.B.I. and we find that on the first page there is also 
an endorsement to the said effect by the seizing officer. 
In the aforesaid two registers also the name of the 
appellant does not find place.
9. Learned counsel for the university has also 
produced before us the tabulation register of B.Ed. 
examination in which name of the appellant finds place.
10. All the registers were shown to Shri Sandeep 
Kothari, learned counsel for the appellant but he could 
not point out to any other material which is worth 
noticing or contrary to what has been recorded above. 
He, however, prays for and is granted two weeks’ time to 
file affidavit of the appellant and bring on record 
therewith the photocopies of the marksheets of different 
examinations alleged to have been passed by the 
appellant and on the basis of which he secured his 
appointment on the post of Junior Lecturer.
11. List thereafter.
12. The original registers have been returned to learned 
counsel for the appellant and he undertakes to place on 
record the relevant part of the endorsement on the 
tabulation register by the officer who carried out the 
seizure and the relevant part of the tabulation register of 
B.Ed. examination where the name of the appellant 
figures. As in the other registers, the name of the 
appellant does not find place, therefore, photocopies of 
the other registers need not be filed.
(Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.)
